description.content: Recompute row heights and offsets after the specified index (defaults to 0). Table has no way of knowing when its underlying list data has changed since it only receives a rowHeight property. If the rowHeight is a number it can compare before and after values but if it is a function that comparison is error prone. In the event that a dynamic rowHeight function is in use and the row heights have changed this function should be manually called by the "smart" container parent. This method will also force a render cycle (via forceUpdate) to ensure that the updated measurements are reflected in the rendered table.

description.content: Scroll to the specified vertical offset; scrollLeft is ignored (tables don't scroll horizontally). Offsets are clamped to the scrollable range. This allows a Table to be used with ScrollSync. Useful for animating position changes. If the Table has a scrollElement, the scroll element (e.g. the window) is scrolled instead.

methods.name: scrollToPosition

description.content: Ensure the row at the specified index is visible (scrolling if necessary). This method can be used to safely scroll back to a row that a user has scrolled away from even if it was previously scrolled to. The align parameter (default "auto") controls the alignment of the row: "auto" scrolls the least amount possible to ensure that the specified row is fully visible (a row taller than the table is aligned to its start, so that its start is visible); "start" aligns the row to the top of the table and "end" to the bottom; "center" aligns it in the middle. This is a one-time scroll: the row is not kept in view afterwards (e.g. if the table's size or its row heights change). Rows that haven't been measured yet (e.g. by CellMeasurer) are positioned using their estimated heights. If the Table has a scrollElement, the scroll element (e.g. the window) is scrolled instead.
